currentContext.business: The Company develops and sells real estate in India, having 'built a strong reputation for delivering successful projects and setting industry benchmarks across asset classes, including pioneering retail developments, world-class commercial spaces and premium residential complexes'. Its FY2025-26 business was led by the residential segment, which 'remained the principal contributor to the Company's business', alongside plotted development described as 'one of the Company's core business verticals and an important driver of future growth' across MMR, Pune, Karjat, Alibaug and other emerging growth corridors, plus a commercial segment serving technology companies, Global Capability Centres and financial services firms. A key structural change is the operationalisation of the real estate development platform established in June 2024 with Alpha Alternatives Group and Delta Group, whose first project 'Peninsula Estates - Alibaug ONE' has been launched and under which 'several additional projects ... are in advanced stages of planning and are expected to be launched over the next 8-12 months'. NOTE: this bundle carried three primary-financial tables (MD&A '5. FINANCIAL REVIEW', the Directors' Report '1. FINANCIAL RESULTS' summary and Form AOC-1 Part A/Part B), plus the share-capital table, the '6. REVIEW OF PERFORMANCE' revenue/PAT lines and the related-party outstanding-balance note; none of those figures have been extracted anywhere in this file, by design.

PLATFORM: pursuant to the Joint Venture Agreement dated June 24, 2024 (approved by shareholders at the EGM held June 03, 2024) to form a Real Estate Platform with the Real Estate 2.0 Residential Opportunities Fund (a scheme of Alpha Alternatives Special Situations Fund, 'Alpha AIF') and Delta Corp Limited ('Delta'), the Company invested during the year - through its wholly owned subsidiary Peninsula Holdings and Investments Private Limited (PHIPL) - into the capital of three platform entities, each alongside corresponding investments by Alpha AIF and Delta: M/s. Zenithvista Real Estate LLP (Deed of Reconstitution executed January 27, 2026). The platform was operationalised during the period and launched its first project, 'Peninsula Estates - Alibaug ONE' in Alibaug; 'several additional projects under this platform are in advanced stages of planning and are expected to be launched over the next 8-12 months'. EXECUTION: 'significant progress on execution/completion and handover of ongoing Pune projects Peninsula Centre (OC Received), Peninsula Plaza (launched), Ashok Vistas, Ashok Vann and Address One'. risks.note: Listed first among the MD&A 'Threats / Risks': 'Changes in regulatory environment'. The Directors' Report reinforces it - 'many types of risks ... emerge on a regular basis due to many factors such as changes in regulatory framework, economic fundamentals etc.' For a Mumbai redevelopment-led strategy the regulatory surface is unusually wide and live: DCPR 2034 and Regulation 33(5) FSI / Transit-Oriented Development incentives, the society-consent threshold cut from 70% to 51%, MHADA's new power to take over stalled or unsafe cessed buildings, and a mandatory 20% bank guarantee of total project cost imposed on developers to prevent defaults - a direct working-capital and bonding cost the AR states as a rule.

risks.risk: Input cost volatility squeezing project margins
risks.note: MD&A 'Threats / Risks' lists 'Volatility in input costs', and the redevelopment section is explicit: 'Rising costs for raw materials (cement, steel, finishing goods) and labour are squeezing margins. So efficient project management, timely delivery are the key differentiators between competing developers.' The Company's mitigation is execution discipline, not contractual pass-through - no cost escalation clause, hedge or fixed-price arrangement is disclosed.

Listed among the MD&A 'Threats / Risks'. It cuts twice for this Company - through home-buyer affordability and financing conditions (the residential segment is described as driven by 'sustained end-user demand and stable financing conditions'), and through its own leverage, where the long-term loan / Lease Rental Discounting facility rating moved from 'CARE BBB- Stable' to 'CARE BB+ Stable' during FY 2025-26 (rating trajectory back-filled from the sibling capex_expansion bundle).

Listed among the MD&A 'Threats / Risks' as 'macroeconomic uncertainties including residual geopolitical risks'. The MD's letter frames the year as one of 'heightened global geopolitical uncertainty, particularly the continuing conflict in West Asia, which has impacted global trade flows, commodity prices, and investor sentiments', with 'transient concerns on demand and pricing' in the Company's own markets.

risks.risk: Project viability risk from aggressive bidding and escalating society demands in redevelopment
risks.note: Stated verbatim as a cost/viability vector 'that need to be managed': 'Premium expectations from housing societies (demanding disproportionately larger corpus funds and substantial extra carpet area) coupled with reckless financial bidding by non-local developers are creating severe project viability risks.' This is the sharpest company-relevant risk in the document because Mumbai redevelopment is a vertical the Company is actively entering, having acquired projects and readied them for launch.

risks.risk: Geographic and segment concentration - MMR and Pune, residential-led
risks.note: Structural, though not labelled a risk. The Company's markets are the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Mumbai redevelopment, Pune, Karjat and Alibaug; MMR redevelopment activity is itself concentrated, with 'the Western Suburbs (Bandra to Borivali) command a massive 75%+ share of the total redevelopment activity'. Revenue depends on the residential segment, which 'remained the principal contributor to the Company's business during FY 2025-26'. No export, customer-count or single-customer concentration disclosure exists (a developer sells to retail buyers), and no BRSR concentration table was supplied.

risks.risk: Credibility / delivery-track-record risk in a market that now excludes weaker developers
risks.note: The AR states buyers 'exclusively prefer buying free-sale components from institutional, Grade-A developers with proven credibility, avoiding unorganized, small-scale developers' due to historic delays. This is written as an industry tailwind for established players, but it is symmetrical: any slippage on 'efficient execution and timely delivery' (a stated Looking Ahead priority) directly costs saleability. Affordability is also narrowing - 'the middle class is increasingly being priced out of core suburban locations into peripheral regions.'

risks.risk: Data protection, information security and process-control risk
risks.note: The Company treats this as material enough to launch a named programme: 'the Company has launched a comprehensive internal initiative titled PROTECT PLL 360 ... designed to build awareness, strengthen organizational practices, and embed a culture of security and accountability into everyday operations', to 'enhance data protection, reinforce compliance standards, and promote responsible business practices'. Internal controls extend to construction-material quality - 'particular emphasis is placed on ensuring that materials deployed at construction sites are subjected to appropriate quality testing and verification procedures before use.'

risks.risk: Sector-inherent uncertainty managed through a non-committee risk framework
risks.note: The Directors' Report states 'the Company is exposed to inherent uncertainties owing to the sector in which it operates' and relies on 'a risk management framework through internal audit process', with key risks and mitigation actions 'discussed at the Audit Committee'. The MD&A describes 'an internally constituted risk management task team ... [which] conducts need-based reviews' - i.e. need-based rather than periodic, and no separate Risk Management Committee, risk register or ERM heat-map is disclosed in the routed text.

The joint venture HEM Infrastructure and Property Developers Private Limited is listed as 'under CIRP w.e.f. July 14, 2025'. Back-filled from the Directors' Report in the sibling profile bundle - the risks_esg bundle carries no such disclosure. The Company itself states 'there are no proceedings initiated/ pending against the Company under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016'.
